<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Design decisions will significantly alter the implementation plan.

Four open questions shape the implementation. Hot coloring may conflict with manual colors. Fade duration is undecided. Scope is tree view only. Backfilling existing tags is unresolved.

Hot tags fade to the default ThemeIcon once they grow old enough. The interaction between hot coloring and manual `setTagColor` is the critical question to resolve. A sensible default for fade duration should be chosen. Creation dates should be stamped either when a tag is first added via `addCellTag`, or when it first appears in a notebook scan.

Tags created outside the extension API—such as through manual JSON edits or imports—must remain cold. Stamping creation dates on first discovery would incorrectly heat up existing tags. Brand-new tags appearing during a session could receive a fresh timestamp, though that logic is difficult to implement cleanly.

A `createdAt` field will be added to `TagProperties`. Existing tags missing this field will stay cold. Stamping will happen inside `addCellTag` and similar creation paths. Renames will preserve the original timestamp.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I have enough information to create a solid plan.

Manual colors override hot colors. A one-month fade window applies to hot colors. Existing tags without timestamps remain cold. The implementation adds `createdAt` to TagProperties, stamps it on first creation, and derives hot colors from age when no manual color exists.

Periodic refreshes will cool colors over time. A configurable fade duration defaults to 30 days. Tooltips will display the tag's creation date and age. Hot colors fade from opaque red toward transparent, then switch to the default tag icon once fully cooled. A helper function will compute the current color based on age.

The helper computes tag age by subtracting the stored timestamp from the current time, clamps it to the fade window, and interpolates a red color with alpha from opaque to transparent. Stamping should happen inside `TagPropertiesManager.ensureCreatedAt` or `addCellTag`, including tags added through execution tracking. Renamed tags already carry their creation timestamp because the rename copies properties.

Raw edits outside the extension will stay clear until the extension adds the tag. The periodic refresh can run every fifteen to thirty minutes, or trigger on tree view visibility changes. Sorting by creation date was not requested, so the change remains focused on coloring.

Scope stays limited to coloring. A settings toggle for the fade duration and an enabled flag will be added, defaulting to thirty days.
</details></think>

Persist creation time\n\nExtend [`src/models/tagProperties.ts`](src/models/tagProperties.ts):\n\n```typescript\ncreatedAt?: string; // ISO 8601\n```\n\nIn [`src/cellTags/cellTags.ts`](src/cellTags/cellTags.ts) `addCellTag`, after collecting `newTags`, for each new tag name that has **no** existing `createdAt` in notebook `tagProperties`, call `TagPropertiesManager.setTagProperties` with `{ ...existing, createdAt: new Date().toISOString() }`.\n\nThis covers add-tag commands, multi-cell add, and execution-tracking tags (all go through `addCellTag`). Rename already copies properties, so `createdAt` is preserved.\n\nAdd a small helper on [`TagPropertiesManager`](src/tagProperties/tagPropertiesManager.ts), e.g. `ensureCreatedAt(notebook, tagName)`, to keep stamp logic in one place.\n\n### 2. <think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The configuration listener references `treeDataProvider`, which is defined earlier in the code. This ordering is safe.

The hot color refresh was added after treeView. `addTagsToMultipleCells` handles duplicate tags across cells correctly by stamping `createdAt` only once per tag.

Legacy tags already present in the notebook will remain cold. `ensureCreatedAt` only stamps `createdAt` when it is absent, so existing tags are not re-stamped.

A subtle bug was found: applying a legacy tag to a new cell currently stamps `createdAt` because `newTags` is non-empty. The plan requires checking notebook-wide `tagProperties` instead, so legacy tags remain cold.

Only tags that appear for the first time in the notebook should receive a `createdAt` stamp. This prevents legacy tags from being incorrectly marked hot when added to new cells.

The plan's implementation is correct. Backfilling legacy tags onto new cells would violate the rule against stamping on open. The edge case is rare enough to leave as-is.

The fix adds a notebook-wide existence check before stamping `createdAt`. A tag only receives a creation timestamp when it does not already appear on any other cell.

The fix checks only other cells for the tag name, excluding the current cell. This works before or after `updateCellTags` because the current cell lacks the new tags during the check. A tag is stamped only if it is completely new to the notebook; existing legacy tags remain cold.
</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Reviewed and hardened. A few real problems showed up:

**Launch**
- [`.vscode/launch.json`](.vscode/launch.json) pointed `--python-interpreter` at a non-existent `VSCODE_EXTENSIONS\...` path. Unknown CLI args can be treated as files to open and stall the Extension Host. Updated to `${workspaceFolder}\examples\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`.

**Feature / activation reliability**
- `getAllTagProperties` returned a **live** metadata object and mutated it in place before saving — that can fail on frozen metadata or fail to persist `createdAt`. It now **clones** first.
- Hot color used `rgba(...)` in SVG fills (flaky in tree icons). Switched to `#e74c3c` + `fill-opacity`.
- `ensureCreatedAt` failures are caught so they can’t break tag-add.
- Recompiled so `out/noteAllTags/tagHotColor.js` is present (missing compiled module would make activation fail with `Cannot find module './tagHotColor'`).

**How to verify**
1. F5 with the **Extension** launch config (let the watch/`compile` preLaunch finish).
2. Add a **new** tag name on a notebook cell → All Notebook Tags icon should be hot red.
3. Existing tags without `createdAt` stay the default tag icon (by design).
